title: Fix leader lease leak and safe redispatch for cross-region split-brain
creator: Aisha Gupta
root_cause_summary: A leader-lease renewal path in the routing/placement service failed to persist fence tokens during a rapid geo failover. This allowed two regional controllers to believe they held leadership for overlapping tenant shards, producing duplicate dispatches and KV-cache divergence when traffic was shifted. A separate capacity-evaluation bug caused the dedicated autoscaler circuit-breaker to incorrectly block immediate rehomes, compounding request failures for high-priority customers.
description:
Summary:
During a staged cross-region failover drill (and in one production incident), some tenants experienced duplicated requests, elevated 5xx rates, and persistent KV-cache mismatches after being moved between regions. Investigation shows a leader-lease 'leak' where lease owner metadata (fencing token + last-applied index) was not atomically persisted before accepting new dispatches. When an operator triggered traffic redirection, the previous region retained the ability to accept and serve requests for a short window, causing split-brain behavior for stateful shard routing.

Scope and services affected:
- placement-router (routing/lease manager)
- tenant-dispatcher (request fanout)
- kv-cache sync service
- dedicated autoscaler circuit-breaker
- hosted routing control-plane (traffic planner)

Why this matters:
- Customers see duplicate charges and inconsistent responses (bad for correctness and billing).
- KV-cache divergence leads to cache poisoning and prolonged reconciling work.
- Dedicated customers reported inability to complete tenant rehomes because autoscaler refused new allocations under incorrect capacity assumptions.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- Rolled out emergency feature-flag that enforces serialized lease handoff (synchronous persist + ack) to hosted control plane in region us-east-1 (hotfix runtime-2.4.0-hotfix-leases).
- Temporarily disabled aggressive asynchronous rehome path for Dedicated tenants to force coordinated quiesce and manual handoffs for impacted customers.
- Opened high-priority support tracks and notified 3 impacted customers with instructions and ETA.
acceptance_criteria: Lease handoff persists fencing token atomically and is observable in placement-router metrics
No duplicate dispatches seen during controlled cross-region failover test (synthetic workload) after fix
KV-cache reconciliation completes deterministically within 5 minutes for moved tenants in test run
Dedicated autoscaler no longer blocks valid rehomes under expected load profiles
Feature flag controls exist to opt-in/out and are exercised in canary before global rollout
Runbook updated and validated with SRE playbook run
runbook_steps: 1) PREP: Identify tenant IDs involved, confirm current lease owners via placement-router /debug/leases endpoint
2) QUIESCE: Set tenant routing to maintenance-mode to stop new sessions (route=maintenance), allow inflight requests to drain (max 60s default)
3) SNAPSHOT: Trigger KV-cache snapshot for tenant; store snapshot in temporary S3 bucket (path noted in ticket) for later replay
4) PERSIST HANDOFF: Execute patched lease handoff API which writes fencing token + last-applied-index atomically to consensus store and waits for 2x region acknowledgements
5) VALIDATE: Confirm only new region shows owner=true, query telemetry to ensure no duplicate dispatches in the last 2m
6) REHOME: Update traffic planner to point to target region and enable normal routing; monitor error rate and latency for 15m
7) HEAL: Replay KV snapshots and run async reconciliation; watch KV-cache mismatch metric until <0.1%
8) ROLLBACK PATH: If errors spike >3x baseline or duplicate dispatches reappear, flip feature-flag to legacy handoff and revert traffic planner (follow emergency rollback playbook ENG-9042)
9) COMMUNICATE: Post status to #incidents, update support ticketing with final status, and send closure email to impacted customers
mitigation: Hotfix runtime-2.4.0-hotfix-leases applied to us-east-1 hosted control-plane (rolled to canary then full region)
Temporary disablement of async rehome for Dedicated tenants older than 30d without sticky locks
Manual rehome assistance for impacted customers with guarded, single-tenant operation windows
Increased telemetry sampling on lease changes and fencing token writes
rollout_plan: Canary: deploy patched placement-router to 10% control-plane nodes in us-east-1, enable feature-flag=false for half of canaries to validate metrics
Stage: after 2 hours of green metrics, roll to 50% control-plane nodes and enable feature-flag=true for test tenants
Region: if Stage passes for 6 hours, roll to full us-east-1 and enable by default for hosted; notify dedicated teams before enabling for dedicated pools
Dedicated: ship patch to dedicated-manager package and schedule per-customer upgrade windows; support manual opt-in for immediate fixes
Private/on-prem: publish patch release notes and backport instructions; coordinate with Account Execs for installs requiring air-gap support
testing_plan: Unit tests: add atomic persist unit tests for lease handoff path (cover partial-write failure scenarios)
Integration: simulated cross-region failover test with 100 synthetic tenants and KV-cache verification
Chaos: run chaos-monkey test that kills leader immediately after handoff to ensure fencing prevents duplicate leadership
Load: run mixed QPS workload at 2x normal to validate autoscaler circuit-breaker adjustments
Security: smoke SAST for new persistence code path
comments: 2026-02-20 - Aisha Gupta: Created ticket after post-incident triage. Attaching initial logs and timeline. Slack thread #inc-geo-failover-2026-02 referenced.
2026-02-22 - Marco Reyes: Reproduced race locally with dev-cluster; root cause traced to non-atomic write path in placement-router (commit 7a9b3c4). Preparing patch.
2026-02-24 - Sujin Park (SRE): Deployed canary hotfix to us-east-1 and observed duplicate dispatches drop to 0 in canary for the synthetic workload. Monitoring for 24h.
2026-03-02 - Support (Nora Feldman): Communicated interim mitigation steps to Customer A and Customer B; they requested dedicated maintenance windows for rehomes.
2026-03-07 - Security (Rashid Khan): Reviewed patch; no secrets leakage. Flagged potential audit log gaps for leader handoffs; suggested adding audit events. Marked for follow-up.
2026-03-10 - Marco Reyes: Patch merged to main (PR #4892), release branch runtime-2.4.1 created. Scheduling dedicated-manager release and private docs.
2026-03-10 - Aisha Gupta: Updated runbook with rollback thresholds and customer communication template. Assigned follow-ups for postmortem.
postmortem_actions: Add atomic lease persist end-to-end test in CI
Emit structured audit events on every lease handoff and include fencing token in event
Tweak dedicated autoscaler to validate capacity with a short soft-reserve before rejecting rehomes
Create a small internal tool to list and reconcile conflicting leases across regions
Write a customer-facing KB article describing safe rehome expectations and recommended maintenance window
